title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 5): Moody Dick
summary: Part 5 of NH's facecam series attacking YouTuber Jason Blaha ("Bloho"): his claimed YouTube income, steroid hypocrisy, homophobic insults, flip-flopping 'science', and his poor squat, deadlift, overhead press and curl technique. NH argues the man needs to leave YouTube and get help, and uses him to explain several form errors.
claims: NH avoids using the target's footage or real name so the videos cannot be taken down by copyright or content ID claims
YouTube ad revenue was decent around 2014-15 but has dried up; creators stay anyway because there is no competing platform, and sponsorships replaced ads
Calling out natural status is hypocritical if you are on steroids or TRT yourself; if you criticise others for not being natural, be natural
Naming a person when criticising is an ego trip for clicks; just criticise the practice, since fans won't be convinced and others don't need the name
The claim that homophobes are secretly gay makes no sense, like saying arachnophobes secretly desire spiders
Many gay men follow bodybuilding because it celebrates the male body, but most bodybuilders are straight men pursuing a male power fantasy, like admiring a statue
Natural bodybuilding is the opposite of a toxic death cult: it is life, youth and health
Adding bands and chains to a stalled bench does not make it a PR; at a meet you cannot swap bar weight for bands
Fitness YouTubers are dogmatic because their brand needs to sell something
'Science-based' programs are mostly marketing: people distrust fake natties but not science, so creators google a study that backs the program they sell
Hips shooting up out of the squat hole and good-morning the weight up comes from a weak core, weak thoracic extension and weak glutes
A squat with a curved bar, bands, chains, a box or above parallel would not pass in a powerlifting meet
Box squats are not great for hypertrophy nor for carryover to the regular squat
Deadlifting with a rounded back is only defensible for elite lifters pulling big weights for their bodyweight; otherwise it damages the spine over time
On overhead press and bench the wrists should be stacked over the forearm, not cocked back; a bent-back wrist is a recipe for wrist injury
NH says many people told him they got wrist injuries following that overhead press tutorial
Curling with overextended elbows and shrugging the shoulder turns the curl into a compound movement, moving more weight but stimulating the biceps less
Synthol-damaged biceps cannot be fixed by training
Sloppy heavy lateral raises cause shoulder impingement
A skull crusher that moves the shoulder, elbow and wrist becomes a pullover-like compound move and recruits the triceps less than you think
8-12 reps on the squat is tough and taxing, which lazy lifters avoid
You cannot grow your chest with only chin-ups and overhead press as a minimalist program
A deadlift with plates that are not verified, at a gym with witnesses or on a platform, does not count
exercises: go to depth; brace core, extend thoracic spine and drive with glutes so hips don't shoot up
box, bands and curved bar hide weaknesses
not great for hypertrophy or carryover to the normal squat
rounded back damages the spine for non-elite lifters
stack the wrists, don't let them cock back
don't overextend or shrug; keep it an isolation movement
cheating shifts work away from biceps
moving shoulder and wrist turns it into a pullover
